title: Coal and Petroleum
description: Grade 8 Science: exhaustible and inexhaustible natural resources, fossil fuels, coal and its products, petroleum refining and its fractions, natural gas and conservation.

topics.title: Natural Resources and Fossil Fuels
topics.concept:
The materials we obtain from nature are natural resources. They are of two kinds, depending on how much is available.

  • Inexhaustible (renewable) resources are present in unlimited amounts and will not run out by human use — for example, sunlight and air.
  • Exhaustible (non-renewable) resources are present in limited amounts and can be used up — for example, coal, petroleum, natural gas, minerals and forests.

Coal, petroleum and natural gas are called fossil fuels because they were formed from the dead remains of living organisms (plants and animals) that were buried deep under the Earth millions of years ago. Under great heat and pressure, and in the absence of air, these remains slowly changed into fuels.

Because fossil fuels took millions of years to form and are being used up rapidly, they are exhaustible and will not last forever. This is why we must conserve them — use them carefully and avoid wasting them — so that they are available for the future.

examples.problem: Example 1: Classify these as exhaustible or inexhaustible: sunlight, coal, air, petroleum.
examples.solution:
Inexhaustible resources do not run out; exhaustible ones do.

  • Inexhaustible: sunlight, air.
  • Exhaustible: coal, petroleum.
examples.answer: Inexhaustible: sunlight and air. Exhaustible: coal and petroleum.

examples.problem: Example 2: Why are coal and petroleum called fossil fuels?
examples.solution:
Think about how they were formed.

  • They formed from the dead remains of plants and animals.
  • These were buried for millions of years under heat and pressure.
examples.answer: Because they were formed from the dead remains of living organisms buried deep under the Earth for millions of years.

examples.problem: Example 3: Why must fossil fuels be conserved?
examples.solution:
Consider how fast they form and how fast we use them.

  • They took millions of years to form.
  • They are being used up fast and are exhaustible, so they will run out.
examples.answer: Because they are exhaustible — they took millions of years to form but are being used up quickly, so they will run out.

recap:
• Inexhaustible resources (sunlight, air) will not run out; exhaustible resources (coal, petroleum, minerals) can be used up.
  • Fossil fuels (coal, petroleum, natural gas) formed from dead remains of organisms buried for millions of years.
  • Fossil fuels are exhaustible and must be conserved.

quiz.q: Which of these is an inexhaustible natural resource?
quiz.explanation: Sunlight is inexhaustible; the others are exhaustible fossil fuels.

quiz.q: Coal, petroleum and natural gas are called:
quiz.explanation: They formed from fossils (dead remains), so they are fossil fuels.

topics.title: Coal and Its Products
topics.concept:
Coal is a hard, black solid fossil fuel. It was formed from the remains of large trees and forests that were buried under the soil millions of years ago. The slow process by which dead vegetation became coal under heat and pressure is called carbonisation. Coal is mainly made of carbon.

Coal is widely used as a fuel for cooking, in railways (in the past) and especially in thermal power stations to produce electricity, and in industries. But coal is much more than just a fuel — when it is heated strongly in the absence of air (a process called destructive distillation), it gives several useful products:

  • Coke — a tough, porous, almost pure form of carbon. It is used in the extraction of metals (such as iron) and as a clean fuel.
  • Coal tar — a thick, black, smelly liquid. It is a mixture of about 200 substances and is used to make dyes, paints, explosives, perfumes, plastics, medicines and roofing materials. (The black material used to make roads, called bitumen, is a petroleum product that has now largely replaced coal tar for road surfacing.)
  • Coal gas — a gas obtained during the processing of coal. It was once used for street lighting and is now used as a fuel in industries.

examples.solution:
It is the natural process that forms coal.

  • It is the slow conversion of dead vegetation into coal.
  • It happens under heat and pressure over millions of years.
examples.answer: Carbonisation is the slow process by which buried dead vegetation turns into coal under heat and pressure.

examples.problem: Example 2: Name the product of coal that is almost pure carbon and used to extract metals.
examples.solution:
One coal product is a tough, porous form of carbon.

  • It is coke.
  • Coke is used in extracting metals such as iron.
examples.answer: Coke — a porous, almost pure form of carbon used in extracting metals.

examples.problem: Example 3: Give two useful things that can be made from coal tar.
examples.solution:
Coal tar is a source of many substances.

  • Dyes and paints.
  • Perfumes, explosives, medicines or plastics (any two).
examples.answer: Coal tar is used to make dyes and paints (also perfumes, medicines, explosives, plastics).

recap:
• Coal is a black solid fossil fuel made mainly of carbon, formed by carbonisation of buried forests.
  • It is used as a fuel and in thermal power stations to make electricity.
  • Heating coal in the absence of air gives coke (extracting metals), coal tar (dyes, paints, medicines) and coal gas (industrial fuel).

quiz.q: The slow process that converts dead vegetation into coal is called:
quiz.explanation: Carbonisation is the conversion of buried vegetation into coal.

quiz.q: Which product of coal is an almost pure form of carbon used to extract metals?
quiz.explanation: Coke is a porous, almost pure carbon used in metal extraction.

topics.title: Petroleum, Natural Gas and Conservation
topics.concept:
Petroleum is a dark, oily liquid fossil fuel. It was formed from the dead remains of tiny sea plants and animals that settled at the bottom of the sea, were covered by sand and clay, and changed into petroleum over millions of years. Because petroleum is so valuable, it is often called black gold.

Petroleum taken from the ground (crude oil) is a mixture and is not useful as it is. It is separated into useful parts at an oil refinery by a process called refining (fractional distillation), which separates the mixture based on different boiling points. The separated parts, called fractions, include: petroleum gas (LPG, for cooking), petrol (fuel for cars), diesel (for trucks and trains), kerosene (for stoves and lamps, and as jet fuel), lubricating oil (to reduce friction), paraffin wax (candles, polishes) and bitumen (for surfacing roads).

Natural gas is another important fossil fuel, found above petroleum in the ground. It is a clean fuel and easy to transport through pipes. CNG (Compressed Natural Gas) is used to run vehicles and causes less pollution than petrol or diesel; natural gas is also used to make fertilisers and other chemicals.

Since these fuels are exhaustible and burning them pollutes the air, we must conserve them. We can save fuel by walking or cycling for short trips, using public transport, switching off engines at traffic lights, keeping vehicles serviced, and using clean fuels like CNG and renewable sources where possible. In India, the Petroleum Conservation Research Association (PCRA) advises people on saving fuel.

examples.solution:
The name reflects its appearance and value.

  • It is a dark (black), oily liquid.
  • It is extremely valuable because so many useful products come from it.
examples.answer: Because it is a dark, oily liquid that is extremely valuable, like gold.

examples.problem: Example 2: Name the process used to separate the useful fractions of petroleum, and one fraction used as fuel in homes for cooking.
examples.solution:
Crude oil is separated at a refinery.

  • The process is refining (fractional distillation).
  • LPG (petroleum gas) is used for cooking at home.
examples.answer: The process is refining (fractional distillation); LPG is used for cooking at home.

examples.problem: Example 3: Suggest two ways a family can conserve petrol and diesel.
examples.solution:
Fuel is saved by using vehicles wisely.

  • Walk, cycle or use public transport for short trips.
  • Switch off the engine at red lights and keep the vehicle serviced.
examples.answer: Use public transport/cycle for short trips and switch off the engine at traffic lights (keeping the vehicle well-serviced).

recap:
• Petroleum ('black gold') is an oily liquid fossil fuel formed from sea organisms over millions of years.
  • Crude oil is separated at an oil refinery by refining into fractions: LPG, petrol, diesel, kerosene, lubricating oil, wax, bitumen.
  • Natural gas (CNG) is a clean fuel for vehicles and a raw material for fertilisers.
  • Fossil fuels are exhaustible and polluting, so we must conserve them (PCRA advises on this).

quiz.q: The process of separating petroleum into useful fractions is called:
quiz.explanation: Refining (fractional distillation) separates crude oil into fractions.

quiz.q: Which clean fossil fuel is used to run vehicles with less pollution?
quiz.explanation: CNG is a cleaner fuel that causes less pollution than petrol or diesel.

questions.q: Resources present in unlimited amount that will not run out are called:
questions.explanation: Inexhaustible resources, like sunlight and air, do not run out.

questions.q: Coal, petroleum and natural gas were formed from:
questions.explanation: Fossil fuels formed from the dead remains of plants and animals.

questions.q: Coal is mainly made of the element:
questions.explanation: Coal is mostly carbon.

questions.q: The slow process of conversion of dead vegetation into coal is:
questions.explanation: Carbonisation forms coal from buried vegetation.

questions.q: An almost pure form of carbon obtained from coal, used to extract metals, is:
questions.explanation: Coke is a porous, nearly pure carbon used in metal extraction.

questions.q: Dyes, paints and medicines can be made from which product of coal?
questions.explanation: Coal tar is a mixture used to make dyes, paints, medicines and more.

questions.q: Petroleum is often called:
questions.explanation: Petroleum is called 'black gold' because it is a dark, valuable liquid.

questions.q: The separation of petroleum into useful fractions is called:
questions.explanation: Refining (fractional distillation) separates crude oil into fractions.

questions.q: Which fraction of petroleum is used as fuel in cars?
questions.explanation: Petrol is the fraction used to run cars.

questions.q: Which petroleum product is used for surfacing roads?
questions.explanation: Bitumen is used to make road surfaces.

questions.q: LPG obtained from petroleum is mainly used for:
questions.explanation: LPG (petroleum gas) is used as cooking fuel.

questions.q: CNG stands for:
questions.explanation: CNG is Compressed Natural Gas, a clean vehicle fuel.

questions.q: Natural gas is considered a good fuel because it:
options: Is clean and easy to transport by pipe
questions.explanation: Natural gas burns cleanly and can be piped easily.

questions.q: Fossil fuels must be conserved because they are:
questions.explanation: Fossil fuels are exhaustible, so they must be used carefully.

questions.q: In India, the organisation that advises people on saving petroleum products is:
questions.explanation: PCRA (Petroleum Conservation Research Association) advises on fuel conservation.

questions.q: Why does it take care over thousands of years to use coal and petroleum 'sustainably', unlike sunlight?
options: They take millions of years to form and cannot be quickly replaced
questions.explanation: Fossil fuels form over millions of years, so they cannot be replaced on a human timescale.

questions.q: Different fractions of petroleum (petrol, diesel, kerosene) are separated during refining because they have different:
questions.explanation: Fractional distillation separates the fractions according to their different boiling points.

questions.q: Switching to CNG buses in a city mainly helps to:
questions.explanation: CNG burns more cleanly than petrol or diesel, reducing air pollution.

questions.q: Coke is preferred over raw coal in extracting iron because coke:
options: Is a purer, hotter-burning form of carbon
questions.explanation: Coke is almost pure carbon and burns to give a strong reducing action for extracting metals.

questions.q: A driver who switches off the engine at a long red light is practising:
questions.explanation: Switching off the engine saves fuel, which is fuel conservation.

questions.q: Burning fossil fuels adds carbon dioxide to the air. Too much of it is a problem because it:
questions.explanation: Carbon dioxide from burning fuels is a greenhouse gas that contributes to global warming.
